paragraphs: Look at the two men in this passage, friend. Jesus is bound and slapped in the face, and He still talks plain: "I have spoken openly to the world" (John 18:20). He even asks the officer, "But if I spoke correctly, why did you strike Me?" (John 18:23). Meanwhile Peter is standing by a fire, free to walk around, and he says "I am not" (John 18:17, 25).

Here's what I want you to hold onto. Peter had a sword in that garden (John 18:10-11), and now he can't get through a chat by a charcoal fire. That tells me being bold one minute does not mean you'll be bold the next. Jesus knew it, too, because He told Peter at supper what was coming (John 13:38), and the rooster crowed right on time (John 18:27).

So if you've ever said "I am not" when it counted, you're in good company, and I am NOT the one to throw stones. I spent years in a junk drawer, and I wasn't exactly shouting my name from the rooftops. Don't close the book on Peter, friend, because this story isn't over.
